summary: A 1960 tower on Deadman Mountain that replaced a 1938 CCC wooden tower, still staffed by Forest Service volunteers.

facts.design: CL-style cab, 14x14 ft, on a 55 ft tower

access.note: Visit reports and a posted NHLR sign/directions indicate the public can reach and climb the tower; a volunteer is typically on duty.

events.note: Original wooden fire tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
CCC wooden tower replaced by the current 55 ft tower with CL-style 14x14 ft cab and catwalk.
Registered December 17, 1990 as NHLR US 10 / CO 2, nominated by District Ranger Donna L. Hepp and retired USFS volunteer coordinator Robert D. Sullivan.

corrections.proposed: CL-style cab, 14x14 ft, on a 55 ft tower
corrections.evidence: NHLR description: '55' tower with CL style 14' x 14' cab and catwalk was constructed in 1960.' (the source does not state the tower's material)
NHLR description gives the tower as 55 feet tall (16.76 m).
NHLR page (last updated March 24, 2020) states the lookout 'is staffed by volunteers'; a 2004 visit report found a volunteer on duty.

notes_for_editor: No independent source beyond NHLR and the FFLA Colorado list was found in the cache or a quick check; both agree on name, location and standing status (FFLA uses 'Deadman Mountain'). The NHLR page is unusually detailed for a short tower (CCC predecessor, 2004 visit narrative, 2019 condition note, Sprint cell-site encroachment), so confidence is medium rather than low despite having only one substantive source. Worth flagging: do not confuse with the unrelated 'Deadman Mountain Lookout' in Wyoming, which also appears in the raw cache and is a different structure.
